mainQuestionText: In order to determine the speed (v) of transverse waves in a stretched wire using resonance, you are provided a sonometer setup as shown in figure (1). You are also provided with a set of tuning forks.

subQuestions.text: In this experiment the fundamental mode of resonance of the wire is used. What is the reason for this?
subQuestions.answer: Amplitude/Energy/Loudness of vibrating wire is maximum (in fundamental resonance)

subQuestions.text: Draw the wave pattern formed between bridges P and Q on the following figure (2) for fundamental mode of vibration of the wire. Indicate on same diagram by drawing an arrow, the best position, where the paper rider has to be placed and mark it as X.
subQuestions.answer: Diagram showing fundamental mode wave pattern between P and Q, with X marked at the antinode/best position for paper rider. (For the shape 01 mark, marking X - 01 mark)

subQuestions.text: The distance between the bridges in part (b) above is l and the frequency of the tuning fork is f. Write down an expression for the speed (v) of transverse wave in the sonometer wire in terms of l and f.
subQuestions.answer:
v = fλ
λ = 2l
v = 2fl
(for correct final expression award 02 marks)

subQuestions.text: Rearrange the expression in part (c) (i) above to determine the wave speed v by drawing a straight line graph using the set of tuning forks with known frequencies, so that dimension of the gradient to be LT⁻¹.
State the independent and dependent variables of the graph mentioned in (c) (ii) above.
Coordinates of two points selected to determine the gradient of the above graph are (0·002, 22) and (0·004, 42). Here l is measured in cm and f is in Hz. Find the value of wave speed v in m s⁻¹.
subQuestions.answer:
Gradient = v/2
(for identifying the gradient as v/2)
gradient = (0.42-0.22)m / (0.004-0.002)s
v/2 = 0.2 / 0.002
v = 200 m s⁻¹
(disregard the units)

subQuestions.text: Considering the length of the prongs of tuning forks, which tuning fork is the best for taking the first measurement? Give reason for your answer.
subQuestions.answer:
Tuning fork to be used: Smallest tuning fork/Shortest prongs
Reason: Highest frequency is generated by the tuning fork with shortest prongs/highest frequency tuning fork will give the shortest resonance length of the wire.

subQuestions.text: Vibrating directions of two prongs of tuning fork at a given moment is indicated by arrow heads in figure (3). Indicate the vibration direction of particles of stem (S) of the tuning fork at the same moment by drawing an arrow head appropriately on the same figure.
subQuestions.answer: Arrow drawn appropriately on the stem (S) of the tuning fork, indicating vibration direction.

subQuestions.text: Masses 1 kg, 2 kg and 3 kg can be used to stretch the sonometer wire. What is the most suitable mass to be used in the experiment? Give reason for your selection.
subQuestions.answer:
Most suitable mass to be used is 2.0 kg OR 3.0 kg
Reason: Maximum length of the wire for (fundamental) resonance mode can be obtained and percentage/fractional error of length measurement can be minimized with highest tension of the string.

subQuestions.text: If the wire is resonating with frequency f, write down an expression for the amplitude (A) of the wire in terms of f and g when the paper rider just jumps off.
subQuestions.answer:
ω²A = g or 4π²f²A = g
A = g / (4π²f²)

subQuestions.text: Write down a possible error that could happen when determining the resonance length l and action that you would take to minimize it.
subQuestions.answer:
Error: Paper rider jumps off within a range of length on the wire or uncertainty of obtaining the resonance length.
Action: Repeat the measurements for resonance length several times (and obtain the average length) by changing the distance between two bridges for the same tuning fork
